title: Free-Body Diagram
body:
A **free-body diagram** is the setup step for every dynamics problem. Draw one object as a
point, draw every force acting on that object as an arrow from it, and draw nothing else.

```
a block sliding down a ramp

        N ↑ (perpendicular to the ramp surface)
          |
    f ←---●---→ direction of motion        f = friction, opposing the slide
          |
        W ↓ (mg, straight down)
```

Then choose axes, resolve each force into components with [[Vector Components]], and write
$\sum F = ma$ once per direction. On a ramp the axes are usually tilted to lie along and
perpendicular to the surface, which puts the acceleration entirely in one of them.

Three errors account for most lost marks. Including a force the object exerts on something
else, which belongs on the other object's diagram. Inventing a forward force on an object that
is coasting, since [[Newton's Laws]] require no force to maintain motion. Assuming the
[[Normal Force]] equals the weight, which holds only on a level surface with nothing else
pushing vertically.
